narr: An active monsoon surge brought several back-to-back days of thunderstorms producing heavy rain, damaging wind gusts, and hail across the state.
ev: The Iron County Emergency Manager reported up to 2.5 feet of water on streets in Enoch, as well as water breaching into homes. The water was deepest near Homestead Boulevard. Several homes were flooded.
Law enforcement officials reported a debris flow moved through the Pinnacles and Promised Land Resort areas.
Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding in Sunglow Canyon.
A debris flow was reported into the Elk Ridge area.
Hildale Fire Department dispatch personnel reported water flowing over three street crossings. The streets were closed due to the flows.
The Virgin stream gauge on the Virgin River at Virgin spiked from 108 CFS to 2180 CFS, a rise of over 3 feet.

Zion National Park dispatch personnel reported numerous slot canyons experienced flooding, including Pine Creek and Spry Canyon. The Zion automated weather station recorded 1.29 inches of rain in one hour. In addition, the East Fork Virgin stream gauge on the East Fort Virgin River near Springdale recorded a peak flow of 2790 CFS.

Several reports of flash flooding in and around Escalante, including Birch Creek. Storm spotters reported logs and trees floating in the Escalante River just north of Escalante. Time of event coincident with time of first report.
A Zion Nation Park ranger reported significant flash flooding occurred on Taylor Creek at the north end of the Kolob Canyon area of the park during the night.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported 5 inches of debris, mud, and gravel overflowing the Scenic Drive by the Capitol Gorge area. High-flowing water was also reported in a usually dry wash at the end of the Scenic Drive. Scenic Drive was closed beyond Grand Wash.

Washington County dispatch officials reported water over the road on State Route 17 near Toquerville, briefly closing the road. The bridge where water crossed the road is above full grown trees in the creek below, indicating a significant rise in water level.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a rise from 27 CFS to 493 CFS in 15 minutes, a rise of 1.5 feet.
